title: Expired certificate in the TLS handshake
plain_english: A certificate involved in the EAP-TLS/PEAP handshake has expired. If the alert was sent by the client, your RADIUS server certificate is past its notAfter date; in EAP-TLS it can equally be the client certificate that expired. Everything worked yesterday and broke today at the same minute for everyone? This is it.

causes.cause: The RADIUS server certificate expired — every client starts rejecting the handshake at once.
causes.next_check: Run: openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in <server cert> on the file referenced by certificate_file in mods-available/eap.

causes.cause: An individual client certificate expired (EAP-TLS) — one user/device fails while everyone else works.
causes.next_check: Check the expiry of the certificate on the failing device; reissue from your CA / re-enroll via SCEP-Intune-AD CS as applicable.

causes.cause: A wrong clock makes a valid certificate look expired (device that sat in a drawer, VM with broken NTP).
causes.next_check: Verify the date and time on the failing device and on the RADIUS server before reissuing anything.
